reviews.quote: The fiercest competitor for the iPad Pro is home-made. Pros: brute top performance, WiFi very fast, high-quality unibody chassis, USB-C with 10 GBit/s, two external displays possible, good color accuracy (PWM-free), well-balanced speakers, high recycled content. Cons: slow 60 Hz display, battery charging takes time, SoC throttles under sustained load. (NBC review of the iPad Air 13" M4 2026; 11" shares SoC and chassis design.)

praises: 464g with M4 inside — the lightest way to get full current Apple silicon speed, users call it the perfect travel tablet (r/ipad)
Fits in bags where 13" won't; the 11" Magic Keyboard keeps the whole setup under 1kg
12GB unified memory means zero app reloads even with a dozen apps + Stage Manager windows
BBY sale pricing (~$900 tablet) makes it the best promo target of the Air line
Fanless, silent, and its Wi-Fi 7 radio is the same as the Pro's
complaints: 500-nit LCD (100 less than the 13") is noticeably dimmer outdoors
128GB fills fast; external USB-C SSD becomes mandatory for media
60Hz panel — no ProMotion on any Air
$379.99 keyboard is unlit and the 11" version's keys/trackpad feel cramped vs the 13"
iPadOS still lacks desktop-class apps no matter the size

design_philosophy: The 11" Air is the portability end of the 'right iPad for most people': identical M4/12GB silicon to the 13", shed to 464g and a smaller 500-nit panel. This entry tier is the cheapest M4 Air bundle in Canada and the one most often discounted at retail.
rating_notes: Pro score attached from NBC review of the iPad Air 13" M4 2026 (87%, gap-fill 2026-11-24). standouts: Cheapest M4 Air with keyboard in Canada (~$1,379, ~$1,280 on BBY sale)
Best pure-portability tablet in the lineup: 464g, 6.1mm, full current silicon
dealbreakers: 128GB + 500-nit panel: the two cuts that make the 256GB upgrade worth it for most buyers
